title: Blog Editor
htmlContent:
Blog Editor

This screen lets you edit a blog post. All changes are saved only when you click Save Changes - nothing is saved automatically.

Top Bar

The top-right corner has action buttons:

  • Save Changes (orange) - Saves all fields at once: title, content, status, tags, hero image, and publication date
  • Preview - Opens the published post in a new browser tab. Only available when the post status is Published
  • Translation Assistant - Appears only for translation drafts (posts with "[TRANSLATE TO...]" in the title). Guides you through a 3-step translation process using your AI assistant, automatically preserving images.

Fields (top to bottom)

Title - The post headline. This is what readers see first.

Slug (URL) - The URL path for this post. Example: my-blog-post becomes /blog/my-blog-post. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.

Description (SEO) - A short summary shown in search engine results and social media previews. Keep it under 160 characters.

Hero Image

The main image displayed at the top of the post.

  • Click Select Hero Image (or Change Hero Image if one is already set)
  • A dialog opens with two options:
    • Upload new image - Click Choose File to upload from your computer (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, max 5 MB)
    • Select from existing images - Click any image thumbnail to use it

Status & Publication Date

These two fields appear side by side.

Status - Choose the workflow stage:

  • Draft - Work in progress, not visible to readers
  • In Review - Ready for review before publishing
  • Published - Live and visible on the blog
  • Archived - Hidden from the public blog but preserved in the system

Published At - Controls when the post appears on the blog.

  • Click Choisir une date to open the date picker
  • Pick a day on the calendar, then set the time (hours : minutes)
  • Click Définir maintenant to set the current date and time (French timezone)
  • Click Effacer to clear the date

Tags

Colored labels that categorize your post. Click a tag to select it (it gets a ring highlight). Click again to deselect. The count of selected tags is shown below.

If no tags exist, create them first in the Posts tab using Manage Tags.

Featured Post

An orange section that lets you highlight this post in the featured carousel on the blog page.

  • Toggle the switch on to mark as featured
  • Set Featured Order (1 = appears first in the carousel)
  • Toggle off to remove from the carousel

Content

The main body of your post - a rich text editor with a full toolbar. You can format text, insert images, add links, tables, and switch to code view for direct HTML editing.

Language

Shown at the bottom - displays whether this post is in English or French. The language is set when the post is created and cannot be changed here.

Translation Assistant

The Translation Assistant button only appears for posts with "[TRANSLATE TO...]" in the title. It provides a 3-step process:

  1. Extract - Replaces images with [IMAGE 1], [IMAGE 2] placeholders
  2. Translate - Copy the prompt to your AI assistant and get the translated content
  3. Apply - Paste the translation and images are automatically restored

Tips

  • Always click Save Changes after making edits - there is no auto-save
  • Write your Description (SEO) before publishing - it improves search visibility
  • Set a hero image - posts without one look incomplete on the blog page
  • Use Draft while writing, switch to Published only when ready

title: Planned Posts
htmlContent:
Planned Posts

Your blog post backlog. Each entry here becomes one published blog post. Plan what to write, then use "Create Post" to generate it with AI.

Two views

  • List view (default) — A flat list sorted by status (In Progress first, then Planned, Backlog, Published), then by search volume.
  • Grouped view — Posts organized by Topic Group with collapsible sections. Main Guides appear first, Supporting Articles are indented below.

Switch between views using the List / Grouped toggle in the header.

What are Topic Groups?

A Topic Group is a collection of related articles about the same theme. For example, the "Gift Retirement" group contains all articles about retirement gift ideas. Grouping articles this way helps search engines understand your site structure and boosts rankings.

Main Guide vs Supporting Article

  • Main Guide — A broad, comprehensive article that covers the entire topic (e.g. "Retirement Gift Ideas"). This is the anchor of the group.
  • Supporting Article — A focused article that dives deep into one specific angle (e.g. "Best Retirement Gifts for Women"). Supporting articles link back to their Main Guide.

Post Fields

  • Title — The blog post title (becomes the H1)
  • Article Role — Main Guide or Supporting Article
  • Topic Group — Which group of related articles this belongs to
  • Parent Guide — For Supporting Articles: which Main Guide it supports
  • Market — Target audience (France or English)
  • Category — Content category (Photo, Video, Family, Digital, Crafts, Seasonal)
  • Type — Content type (How-To, Storytelling, etc.)
  • Priority — P1 (lowest) to P5 (highest)
  • Status — Backlog, Planned, In Progress, or Published
  • Primary Keyword — Main SEO keyword to target
  • Secondary Keywords — Supporting keywords
  • Content Angle — Unique perspective for the article
  • Description — What the article should cover

Filters

  • Search — Search by title or keywords
  • Article Role — Show only Main Guides or Supporting Articles
  • Topic Group — Show only posts from a specific group
  • Market — Filter by France or English
  • Category — Filter by content category
  • Status — Filter by workflow status
  • Type — Filter by content type
  • Priority — Filter by priority level

Stats Cards

  • Total Posts — All planned posts in your backlog
  • Ready to Write — Posts with "Backlog" status, waiting to be written
  • In Progress — Posts that are "Planned" or "In Progress"
  • Published — Posts that have been published

Actions

  • Plan New Post — Add a new post to your backlog
  • Edit — Modify post details
  • Delete — Remove post (unlinks any published posts)
  • Create Post — Generate a blog post using AI
  • View Posts — See published posts created from this plan

Tips

  • The List view shows your most actionable posts first (In Progress and Planned at the top)
  • Switch to Grouped view to see how your posts relate to each other within Topic Groups
  • Start by creating a Main Guide for each Topic Group, then add Supporting Articles around it
  • Click any row to expand and see full details including SEO data and content guidance
  • Posts with a "Generated Nx" badge have already been used to create published posts

title: AI Creator
htmlContent:
AI Creator

Generate blog posts using AI. This tool creates a structured prompt, which you copy to your AI assistant (e.g., your AI assistant, Claude). Then paste the AI response back to create a fully formatted blog post.

Step 1: Configure Post

Fill in the following fields:

  • Topic - Describe what the blog post should be about (required)
  • Language - English (EN) or French (FR)
  • Status - Choose Draft, In Review, Published, or Archived
  • Published At - Schedule a future date (optional)
  • SEO Keywords - Comma-separated keywords to target (optional)

Click Generate AI Prompt when ready.

Step 2: Copy Prompt to AI

The generated prompt appears in this panel. Click Copy to Clipboard to copy it. Then paste into your AI assistant, Claude, or your preferred AI assistant. The AI will generate a complete blog post in JSON format.

Step 3: Paste AI's JSON Response

Paste the AI's JSON response into the textarea. If there are formatting issues, click Auto-Fix to repair common JSON problems. Then click Validate & Edit Content to preview and edit the content.

Step 4: Refine Your Content

In this step you can:

  • Edit the Post Title
  • Upload a Hero Image from your Image Bank
  • Add Tags to categorize the post
  • Use the rich text editor to refine the content, add tables, or format text

Click Save Blog Post to save. You'll be automatically taken to the Blog Editor for final review.

Tips

  • Be specific with your topic for better results
  • Always review and edit AI content before publishing
  • Use the SEO keywords field - it improves content targeting
  • The generated prompt includes MEMOPYK brand guidelines automatically
  • Start with Draft status and review before publishing

title: Image Bank
htmlContent:
Image Bank

Central library for all blog images and media assets.

Header Buttons

  • Manage Labels ?�� Open the label management dialog to create, rename, or delete color-coded labels for organizing images
  • Upload Images ?�� Upload new images via drag-and-drop or file browser. Supports JPG, PNG, WebP up to 5MB each. Set alt text, category, and labels per image before uploading

Filters

  • Category dropdown ?�� Filter by content category (Photo Organization, Video Memory, Family Storytelling, Digital Organization, Memory Products, Seasonal, General)
  • Usage dropdown ?�� Show All, Unused Only, Used in Posts, Hero Images, or Body Images
  • Search ?�� Find images by filename, alt text, or labels

Image Cards

Each card shows a thumbnail, filename, category badge, file size, and up to 2 color-coded labels. A usage badge in the top-right corner shows:

  • Used in X posts (green) ?�� Image is actively used
  • Unused (gray) ?�� Image is not referenced by any post

Image Actions (hover)

Hover over an image card to reveal three action buttons:

  • View (eye icon) ?�� Open full details: dimensions, file size, category, labels, and a list of blog posts using this image
  • Edit (pencil icon) ?�� Update alt text, category, and labels
  • Delete (trash icon, red) ?�� Remove image from the bank (confirmation required)

Tips

  • Use descriptive filenames and alt text for SEO
  • Compress images before uploading for faster page loads
  • Use labels to organize images across categories ?�� labels have auto-assigned colors
  • Check the Unused Only filter periodically to clean up unused images

title: Why MEMOPYK Cards
htmlContent:
Why MEMOPYK Cards

Manage the "Why MEMOPYK" cards section on the homepage — the value propositions shown to visitors.

What You Can Do

  • Edit card content — title, description, icon
  • Reorder cards — change display sequence
  • Add/remove cards — adjust the number of value propositions

title: Analytics — Video
htmlContent:
Video Analytics

Track how visitors engage with your videos: starts, watch duration, and completion rates.

Metrics

  • Total Views — Number of video play events
  • Unique Viewers — Distinct IPs who watched at least one video
  • Avg Watch Time — Mean seconds watched per view
  • Completion Rate — % of views that reached the end
  • Engagement % — % of all visitors who watched a video

Video Funnel

Select a video from the dropdown to see how viewers progress through milestones (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%).

Top Videos Table

All tracked videos ranked by play count. Columns: plays, avg watch time, 50% reach, completion.

title: Analytics — Blog
htmlContent:
Blog Analytics

Track blog post performance: views, reading patterns, popular topics, and keyword traffic.

Data Source

Toggle between MEMOPYK and GA4 at the top. Blog analytics default to MEMOPYK (internal tracking, admin IPs excluded).

Sections

  • Blog Views Over Time - Area chart showing daily blog post views for the selected period, with total views count
  • Popular Blog Posts - Table of most-viewed posts ranked by view count. Click a row to navigate to the post in the Posts tab
  • Top Content Topics - Topics ranked by total traffic from linked posts. Click to navigate to the Planned Posts tab
  • Top SEO Keywords - Keywords ranked by traffic they drive. Click to filter posts by keyword
  • Category Performance - Bar chart and stats grid showing traffic breakdown by content category

Cross-Navigation

Click any post, topic, or keyword row to jump directly to the related Blog Hub tab with the item highlighted.

title: Analytics — Diagnostics
htmlContent:
System Diagnostics

Server health, database status, and cache usage at a glance.

Status Cards

  • Server - Server health status and version number
  • Database - Connection status and response time
  • Uptime - Time since last server restart
  • Analytics - DB and GA4 pipeline status (ON/OFF badges)

Cache Storage

Shows video cache, image cache, and total usage with a progress bar. Includes file counts and sizes.

Auto-refresh

Health checks refresh every 30 seconds, cache stats every 60 seconds. Click Refresh for an immediate update.

When to Check

Visit this tab if analytics data seems stale or missing - it will show whether the server, database, or cache layer has issues.

title: AI Context (Brand Brain)
htmlContent:
AI Context - Brand Brain

Define the brand personality, tone, and knowledge base that AI uses when generating blog content.

What You See

Context entries are grouped by category:

  • Brand Guidelines - Brand voice, tone, style, and content guidelines
  • Translation Rules - Rules for how AI should handle translations

Each entry shows its key, title, content, and last update timestamp.

How to Edit

  1. Click Edit on any entry card
  2. Modify the content in the text area
  3. Click Save to apply changes

How It Works

When AI generates blog content (via the Posts tab), it reads this context to match your brand voice. The more detailed your context, the better the AI output.

Internal API

The full context (brand + published posts) is available at GET /api/internal/ai-context/full for integration with other tools.

title: Legal Documents
htmlContent:
Legal Document Management

Manage legal pages displayed on the website.

What You Can Do

  • Edit document content in rich text format
  • Bilingual support - separate French and English versions
  • Toggle visibility - activate or deactivate individual documents

Document Types

  • Legal Notice (Mentions legales)
  • Terms of Service (CGU)
  • Terms of Sale (CGV)
  • Privacy Policy (Politique de confidentialite)
  • Cookie Policy (Politique des cookies)
  • Refund Policy (Politique de remboursement)
  • Disclaimer (Avis de non-responsabilite)

title: New Post
htmlContent:
Create a New Blog Post

This is your starting point for creating new content. Choose the method that works best for you:

Write from scratch

Opens the Blog Editor with a blank post. Best when you have a clear idea of what you want to write.

Generate with AI

Uses AI to generate a draft based on your topic and preferences. Great for overcoming writer's block or getting a head start.

💡 Tip: You can always switch methods — start with AI to get a draft, then refine manually in the Blog Editor.

title: Analytics — Overview
htmlContent:
Overview

Key performance indicators at a glance for the selected date range.

KPI Cards

  • Visitors — Unique visitors (by IP)
  • Sessions — Total browsing sessions
  • Page Views — Total page loads across the site
  • Bounce Rate — % of single-page sessions

Top Pages

The most visited pages ranked by view count. Hover for full URLs.

Tips

  • Use the Date Filter toggle to exclude data before your launch date
  • Switch between GA4 and MEMOPYK data sources to compare

title: Analytics — Geography
htmlContent:
Geography

Where your visitors come from — countries, cities, and language breakdown.

Country Distribution

Bar chart showing the top countries by visitor count. Hover for exact numbers.

Language Split

Shows the proportion of FR vs EN sessions. Useful for deciding content priorities.

City Table

Top cities by session count. The "Country" column shows the ISO code.

Tips

  • Use the Language global filter to isolate FR or EN traffic across all tabs
  • Use the Country filter to focus on a single market

title: Analytics — Trends
htmlContent:
Traffic Trends

Visualize how your site traffic changes over time.

Charts

  • Daily Sessions — Line chart of session counts per day
  • Daily Page Views — Line chart of total page views per day
  • New vs Returning — Proportion of first-time vs repeat visitors

Tips

  • Expand the date range to 90 days to spot weekly patterns
  • Use the Language filter to compare FR vs EN traffic trends separately
  • Spikes often correlate with social media posts or email campaigns

title: Blog Hub
htmlContent:
Blog Hub

Your central hub for blog management — from idea to published article.

The Workflow

The tab bar shows your content pipeline as 5 numbered steps:

  1. Keywords — SEO keyword research. Search data that informs what to write about.
  2. Planned Posts — Your blog post backlog. Each entry is a plan for one blog post.
  3. Planner — Schedule when to write and publish on a 12-week calendar.
  4. Posts — Write, edit, publish, and translate blog articles.
  5. Image Bank — Store and manage images for your articles.

The active tab is highlighted in orange with its step number. You don't have to follow the order — click any tab to jump directly.

Default View: Planner

Blog Hub opens on the Planner (step 3) — your daily command center showing what's scheduled this week and what's coming up.

Planned Posts vs Published Posts

A Planned Post (in the Planned Posts tab) is a content plan — the title, keywords, and guidance for an article you intend to write. A Published Post (in the Posts tab) is the actual article that readers see on the blog. One planned post typically leads to one published post.

Post Statuses

  • Draft - Work in progress, not visible to readers
  • In Review - Ready for review before publishing
  • Published - Live and visible on the blog
  • Archived - Hidden from the public blog but preserved

Dashboard Stats

  • Total Posts - All planned posts in your backlog
  • Assigned This Week - Posts scheduled for this week
  • Unassigned - Posts not yet scheduled

title: Analytics — Exclusions
htmlContent:
IP Exclusions

Manage IP addresses excluded from all analytics data, and configure date-based data exclusions.

IP Exclusions

  • Excluded IPs are filtered out from all MEMOPYK analytics queries
  • Both exact IPs and CIDR ranges (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) are supported
  • The IPs: N badge in the analytics header shows the active count

Actions

  • Auto-detect - Detects your current IP address for quick exclusion
  • Add IP - Manually enter an IP or CIDR range with an optional label
  • Toggle - Enable/disable individual exclusions without deleting them
  • Delete - Permanently remove an exclusion entry

Date Exclusion (Since Date)

Set a start date to exclude all analytics data collected before that date. Useful for ignoring pre-launch test data. When active, a Since: [date] badge appears in the analytics header.

Tips

  • Add all team members' IPs to get clean visitor data
  • Labels help remember why an IP was excluded (e.g., "Stephane home", "Office VPN")

title: Analytics — CTA
htmlContent:
CTA Tracking

Monitor clicks on call-to-action buttons: "Book a Call", "Quick Quote", and other CTAs.

Dual Tracking

CTA clicks are sent to both GA4 and the internal Supabase database for reliability. The MEMOPYK source shows Supabase-tracked clicks (admin IPs excluded).

Metrics

  • Total Clicks — All CTA button clicks in the period
  • By CTA Type — Breakdown per button (book_call, quick_quote, etc.)
  • Click Timeline — Daily click trend

Tips

  • Compare GA4 vs MEMOPYK counts — large discrepancies may indicate ad-blocker impact

title: Planner
htmlContent:
Planner

12-week content calendar to plan, schedule, and track your blog production.

Two Views

Planned Posts - Schedule when to write. Assign posts from your backlog to specific days.

Published Posts - See when posts go live. Published posts appear on their publish date, drafts on their assigned date.

Planned Posts View Actions

  • Click + on any day to assign a planned post from your backlog
  • Drag a card to reschedule it to a different day
  • Click on a Planned post to create a published post from it
  • Click to view or edit the associated post
  • Click to remove a planned post from the calendar

Published Posts View Actions

  • Drag a post card to reschedule its publication date
  • Click to view or edit the post

Navigation

  • Use arrow buttons to move 4 weeks forward or back
  • Click Today to jump to the current week

Status Colors

  • Orange border - Planned (no published post yet)
  • Yellow border - Draft or In Review
  • Green border - Published

Tips

  • Aim for 2-3 posts per week for consistent publishing
  • Schedule posts at least 1 week ahead
  • Use the Planned Posts view to plan, then switch to Published Posts view to track progress

title: Analytics — Clarity
htmlContent:
Microsoft Clarity

Heatmaps and session recordings powered by Microsoft Clarity.

Status

Clarity requires a project ID configured in the environment. If the Clarity widget is not loading, check that VITE_CLARITY_PROJECT_ID is set.

What Clarity Provides

  • Heatmaps — See where visitors click, scroll, and hover
  • Session Recordings — Watch anonymized replays of real visits
  • Rage Clicks — Detect frustrated clicking patterns
  • Dead Clicks — Find elements users click that do nothing

Setup

  1. Create a project at clarity.microsoft.com
  2. Copy the project ID
  3. Set VITE_CLARITY_PROJECT_ID in your environment

title: Keywords
htmlContent:
Keywords (12,501)

SEO keywords from Google Keyword Planner, organized for content planning.

Quick Filters

One-click presets for common keyword analysis tasks:

  • 🎯 Quick Wins — Low competition + High intent keywords in Tier 1-2. Your easiest path to conversions. Start here.
  • 📈 Traffic Drivers — High-volume Tier 2 keywords (1,000+ searches/mo). Build authority and brand awareness.
  • 💰 Money Keywords — All high-intent keywords in Tier 1-2, regardless of competition. Your full conversion universe.
  • 🇫🇷 France Priority — French market Tier 1-2 keywords. Focus on your home market advantage.
  • ✍️ Blog Ideas — Medium intent, low-medium competition keywords. Perfect for content calendar planning.
  • ✕ Clear — Reset all filters to default.

Click any preset to instantly apply its filters. The preset deactivates if you manually change any filter.

Filtering

Use the dropdowns above each column to filter:

  • Search — Type to find specific keywords
  • Cluster — Content category (Gift Retirement, VHS Legacy, etc.)
  • Market — 🇫🇷 France or 🇺🇸 US
  • Tier — Relevance to MEMOPYK service
  • Searches/mo — Monthly search volume ranges
  • Comp. — How hard to rank (Low/Medium/High)
  • Intent — Buyer readiness

Each filter supports multi-select: check/uncheck individual options, use Select All to toggle all. Click OK to apply, Cancel to revert.

Table Columns

  • Keyword — The search term. Cluster shown inline as a 🏷️ Gift Retirement tag
  • Market — 🇫🇷 FR = France, 🇺🇸 US = United States
  • Tier — How relevant to MEMOPYK:
    • Tier 1 = Direct service match (best!)
    • Tier 2 = High relevance
    • Tier 3 = Secondary
  • Searches/mo — Monthly search volume from Google
  • Competition — How hard to rank:
    • Low = Easy to rank (good!)
    • Medium = Moderate effort
    • High = Hard to rank
  • Intent — Conversion likelihood:
    • High = Ready to buy (best!)
    • Medium = Comparing options
    • Low = Just researching
  • Planned Posts — Number of planned posts targeting this keyword. Click to view in the Planned Posts tab.
  • Posts — Number of published posts using this keyword. Click to view in the Posts tab.

Actions

  • ✏️ Edit — Modify keyword details
  • 🗑️ Delete — Remove (with confirmation)

Best Strategy

  1. Start with Quick Wins preset — these are your best ROI keywords
  2. Use Traffic Drivers for brand awareness content
  3. Create planned posts targeting these keywords first
  4. Track progress via the Planned Posts and Posts counts

title: Analytics — Live
htmlContent:
Live Visitors

Real-time activity on the site right now.

What You See

  • Active Users - Visitors with activity in the last 5 minutes
  • Current Pages - Which pages are being viewed right now
  • Session Timeline - Recent session starts and page navigations

Auto-refresh

This tab refreshes every 30 seconds automatically. The timestamp shows when data was last fetched.

title: Posts
htmlContent:
Posts

This is where you manage all your blog posts - create, edit, preview, translate, and delete.

Top Buttons

  • New Post (orange, top right) - Opens the creation page where you choose to write from scratch or generate with AI.
  • Manage Tags - Opens a dialog where you can add new tags, rename existing ones, or delete them.

Filters

Use the filter card at the top to narrow your list:

  • Status - Show All Posts, Draft Only, In Review Only, Published Only, or Archived Only.
  • Language - Show All Languages, English, or French.
  • Title Keyword - Type a word to search by post title.
  • The post count on the right shows how many posts match your current filters.

If you arrived from the Planned Posts tab with a filter active, a blue banner appears. Click the X on the badge to clear it.

Post Cards

Each post appears as a card showing:

  • Title - The post name. If created from a planned post, a View source plan link appears next to it.
  • Description - A short summary (2 lines max).
  • Badges below the description: language (EN/FR), status (Draft / In Review / Published date / Archived), tag badges, and Featured (purple) if marked.

Action Icons (right side of each card)

Each card has 5 controls on the right:

  1. Status dropdown - Change status directly (Draft, In Review, Published, or Archived). No need to open the editor.
  2. Eye icon ("View post") - Open the post on the public blog in a new tab.
  3. Translation icon ("Duplicate for translation") - Create a copy for translation. All images are preserved.
  4. Pencil icon ("Edit post") - Open the post in the Blog Editor.
  5. Trash icon ("Delete post", red) - Delete the post with confirmation.

Tips

  • To quickly change a post status, use the Status dropdown on the card - no need to open the editor.
  • The Translation button copies everything (title, content, images). Just replace the text.
  • To create a post from a content plan, go to the Planned Posts tab and click "Create Post" on any entry.
  • Click New Post to choose between writing from scratch or generating with AI.

Translating Posts

Click the 🌐 translate icon on any post to create a translation. Choose ✨ Translate with AI for one-click automatic translation, or Translate manually to use your own tools.

title: Video Gallery
htmlContent:
Video Gallery Management

Manage the portfolio video gallery displayed on the website.

What You Can Do

  • Add/edit/delete gallery video entries
  • Reorder videos by drag-and-drop
  • Set thumbnails and captions for each video
  • Toggle visibility — hide videos without deleting them

Video Sources

Videos can be hosted externally (YouTube, Vimeo) or uploaded directly. The gallery handles caching and proxy delivery automatically.

title: FAQ Management
htmlContent:
FAQ Management

Manage the Frequently Asked Questions displayed on the website.

What You Can Do

  • Create FAQ sections — group related questions together
  • Add/edit/delete questions within each section
  • Reorder sections and questions by drag-and-drop
  • Bilingual support — FAQ content in both French and English

Tips

  • Keep answers concise — visitors scan, they don't read long paragraphs
  • Use questions that match how customers actually ask (good for SEO)

title: CTA Buttons
htmlContent:
CTA Button Management

Manage Call-to-Action buttons displayed across the website.

What You Can Do

  • Edit button text — labels for Book a Call, Quick Quote, etc.
  • Configure destinations — where each CTA button leads
  • Set button styling — colors and visual emphasis

Tracking

CTA clicks are automatically tracked in both GA4 and Supabase. View click analytics in the CTA tab of the Analytics Dashboard.

title: SEO Management
htmlContent:
SEO Management

Configure meta tags, Open Graph data, and page-level SEO settings for the website.

Language Switcher

Use the French / English toggle in the top-right to edit SEO settings for each language separately.

Sub-Tabs

  • Basic SEO - Page title, meta description, keywords, canonical URL, and a Google search result preview
  • Robots - Control indexing, link following, archiving, and snippet behavior
  • Social Media - Open Graph (Facebook, LinkedIn) and Twitter Card settings
  • Advanced - JSON-LD structured data, hreflang alternate languages, and extra meta tags
  • Live Preview - Preview the complete HTML head tags that will be generated

Actions

  • Save SEO Settings - Save your changes (bottom of the form)
  • History - View version history of SEO changes
  • Publish - Publish current settings to the live site

Tips

  • Keep titles under 70 characters and descriptions under 320 characters
  • Each language version should have unique title and description
  • Use the Live Preview tab to verify your tags before publishing

title: Partners Directory
htmlContent:
Partners Directory

Manage the professional digitization partners displayed in the partner directory on the website.

Header Buttons

  • Add Partner — Create a new partner entry manually (opens a 4-tab form: Basic Info, Location, Services, Visibility)
  • Import TSV — Bulk import partners from a tab-separated spreadsheet (paste TSV data with header row)
  • View Map — Open the public partner directory map in a new tab
  • Download Excel — Export all partners as a downloadable spreadsheet

Filters

  • Search — Filter by partner name or city
  • Status dropdown — All, Pending, Approved, or Rejected
  • Type dropdown — All, Digitization, Restoration, or Transfer

Table Columns

  • Date — Submission date (sortable)
  • Partner — Company name (sortable)
  • Type — Service type badge (sortable)
  • Contact — Contact name and email
  • Location — City and country (sortable)
  • Status — Click the badge to cycle: Pending, Approved, Rejected (sortable)
  • Active — Click to toggle Active/Inactive
  • Show on Map — Click to toggle On Map/Hidden
  • Actions — Edit (pencil) and Delete (trash) buttons

Partner Statuses

  • Pending — New submission awaiting review
  • Approved — Visible in the directory
  • Rejected — Not shown to visitors

Edit Partner Form

The edit dialog has 4 tabs:

  • Basic Info — Name, type, status, contact, email/phone visibility, website, description
  • Location — Address, city, postal code, country, latitude/longitude
  • Services — Photo/film/video format checkboxes and delivery methods
  • Visibility — Active toggle, Show on Map toggle, URL slug

title: Analytics Dashboard
htmlContent:
Analytics Dashboard

Track visitor behavior, video engagement, CTA clicks, and blog performance - all from one dashboard.

Tab Navigation

Use the horizontal tabs to switch between analytics views:

  • Overview - KPIs at a glance: visitors, sessions, page views, bounce rate, top pages
  • Live View - Real-time visitor activity on the site right now
  • Trends - Traffic trends over time with daily/weekly breakdowns
  • Video - Video engagement funnel: starts, progress milestones, completions
  • Geo - Visitor geography: countries, cities, language breakdown
  • CTA - Call-to-action button click tracking (Book a Call, Quick Quote)
  • Blog - Blog post views, popular posts, top keywords and categories
  • Clarity - Microsoft Clarity heatmaps and session recordings (coming soon)
  • Fallback - Server health, database status, cache usage
  • Exclusions - Manage IP addresses and date exclusions from analytics

Global Filters

Filters at the top apply across all tabs:

  • Date range - Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or Custom range
  • Language - Filter by ALL, EN, or FR visitors
  • Country - Filter by visitor country (France, US, Canada, UK, etc.)

Data Sources

The Data Source badge shows where numbers come from:

  • MEMOPYK (orange) - Internal Supabase tracking. Admin IPs excluded. Most accurate for conversions.
  • GA4 (blue) - Google Analytics 4. Broader coverage but subject to sampling and consent.

Header Badges

The header shows contextual information:

  • Since: [date] - Appears when the date exclusion filter is active (configured in Exclusions)
  • IPs: N - Shows how many IPs are excluded from analytics

title: Hero Videos
htmlContent:
Hero Video Management

Control the hero video section at the top of the homepage.

Video Management

  • Upload hero videos for the homepage banner (drag-and-drop or file picker)
  • Bilingual videos - set separate videos for French and English, or use the same video for both
  • Set video order - use arrow buttons to control which video plays first
  • Toggle active state - enable/disable individual hero videos

Text Overlays

  • Edit overlay text - headline displayed over the video in both languages
  • Responsive sizes - separate font sizes for desktop, tablet, and mobile
  • Live preview - toggle between French and English preview

title: Travel Agencies
htmlContent:
Travel Agency Management

Manage the travel agency upload portal and agency access codes. Travel agencies receive a unique code, visit the upload page, enter their code, and submit vacation photos/videos for their clients.

Two Sub-Tabs

  • Uploads — Review and manage all client upload submissions
  • Agency Codes — Create and manage the access codes agencies use to upload content

Uploads Tab

Shows all travel upload submissions with Nextcloud folder statistics.

Header buttons:

  • Refresh Stats — Load/reload Nextcloud folder sizes and file counts
  • Refresh List — Reload the submission list from the database

Filters:

  • Search — Filter by client name or email
  • Agency dropdown — Filter by agency code
  • Date range — Start and end date pickers

Table columns (all sortable):

  • Date/Time — When the upload was submitted
  • Client Name — First and last name, plus phone
  • Email — Clickable mailto link
  • Agency — Agency code badge
  • Share Link — Link to the Nextcloud shared folder
  • Status — Success (green) or Failed (red) badge
  • Upload Status — Folder stats (folders, files, size, last upload). Click Load Stats to fetch

Row actions:

  • Mail icon — Resend the confirmation email to the client
  • Trash icon — Delete the submission record (Nextcloud folder must be deleted manually)

Agency Codes Tab

Manage valid agency codes as cards in a grid layout.

Header buttons:

  • Refresh — Reload the agency code list
  • Add Agency Code — Create a new code (agency name, code, email, phone, notes, active toggle)

Each code card shows: Agency name, code (in orange), Active/Inactive badge, contact info, notes, and creation date.

Card actions: Edit (pencil) and Delete (trash) buttons.

Search filters codes by name, code, or email.

title: Cache Management
htmlContent:
Cache Management

Manage the local file cache for all media assets (hero videos, gallery videos, and images). Cached files are served directly from the server for faster page loads instead of fetching from remote storage on every request.

Storage Management Overview

The top card shows overall cache health at a glance:

  • Cache Usage — Current disk usage vs. maximum limit (1 GB), shown as a progress bar with percentage
  • Auto Cleanup — Retention period (30 days) and whether automatic cleanup is enabled
  • Media Files — Total number of cached files and their combined size

Video Sections

Two side-by-side panels show cache status for each video category:

  • Vidéos Hero — Homepage carousel videos (critical for first impression). Shows cache status for each file
  • Vidéos Galerie — Portfolio lightbox videos. Shows cache status for each file

Each section header displays:

  • Production badge — Which server the cache is on
  • X/Y count — Number of cached files out of total expected
  • Update Status — Refresh the cache status for all files in that section

Per-File Status

Each video file row shows:

  • Green checkmark — File is cached and ready to serve
  • Cached (~50ms) green badge — Estimated serve time from cache
  • Download count and last-cached timestamp
  • Refresh Cache — Re-download this specific file from remote storage to update the local cache

Global Cache Actions

Three bulk operation buttons at the bottom of the page:

  • All Media Cache (purple) — Cache all media files (hero videos + gallery videos + images) with full verification. Recommended after each production deployment
  • Smart Cleanup — Remove only expired files (older than 30 days) and orphaned files no longer referenced by any content
  • Images Orphelines — Remove only unused images that are not referenced by any gallery item

Below the buttons: total content count (videos + images) and total cache size.

Tips

  • Run All Media Cache after deploying new video or image content to production
  • Cached files serve in ~50ms vs ~1500ms uncached — keeping the cache warm ensures fast page loads
  • Use Smart Cleanup periodically to free disk space without affecting active content
  • If a video appears outdated on the site, use the per-file Refresh Cache button to re-download it
